newsitem.title: USA: Ill. to unveil financing plan for airport in Nov..
newsitem.headline: Ill. to unveil financing plan for airport in Nov..

text.p: Illinois Department of Transportation plans to release a financial feasibility plan for a proposed new airport southwest of Chicago sometime after the Nov 5 election, a department spokesman said Thursday.
Dick Adorjan said the plan will contain various options for financing and building the facility in Peotone, a town about 35 miles southwest of Chicago.

One financing option under serious consideration is private financing of the airport, which carries an estimated price tag of $2.3 billion. Adorjan said the state plans to initiate talks with private investors about ways the airport can be built privately or through a public-private arrangement.
While general airport revenue bonds have been mentioned for the project, Adorjan said that under a privately developed scenario any revenue bonds that are sold would be taxable.

The airport plan, proposed by Gov. Jim Edgar in 1991, has encountered an uphill battle in winning over airlines. In January 1995, the heads of 16 airlines publicly opposed the project calling it "an unwise and speculative investment in a public facility."
